title: The Negative Verb tm
short: tm "not to be (doing)" negates forms that cannot take n, like infinitives and participles: tm sḏm "not hearing".
trouble: Students skip tm as unknown. It is a helping verb that carries the negation.

blocks.html: The negatives n and nn stand at the head of a clause (Negation with n, nn, "There Is No"). Some forms cannot take them: an infinitive after a preposition, a participle describing a noun, a verb after jr "if". For these Egyptian has a negative verb.

tm "not to do" negates forms that cannot take n: infinitives (r tm sḏm "so as not to hear"), participles (tm sḏm "one who does not hear") and verbs after jr or rdj (jr tm=k sḏm "if you do not listen"). tm takes the form the sentence needs, and the verb after it carries the meaning.

tm is a verb meaning "stop, not do". It can be an infinitive, a participle or a sḏm=f like any other verb, so it slips into places where n cannot go. The verb after it is in a special form Gardiner calls the negatival complement, often written with -w: tm=f sḏm(w). In transliteration many books leave the w in brackets or out.

head: Where
Example
Meaning
rows: he caused me not to hear

blocks.name: eg-glyphs
blocks.cap: The verb that tm negates, here sḏm, follows it: tm sḏm "one who does not hear".

blocks.title: A condition
steps: jr "if" + a verb: here the verb is tm=f, "he does not".
ḏd after it says what he does not do.

blocks.title: Purpose
steps: r + infinitive gives purpose (Purpose and Result).
The infinitive is tm, negated purpose: "so as not to".

blocks.title: After rdj
steps: rdj.n=f + sḏm=f is "he caused that…" (rdj with the sḏm=f).
The sḏm=f is tm=j "I do not", completed by sḏm.

blocks.html: Compare the two ways of saying "not". n sḏm=f "he did not hear" is a main statement, with n at its head. jr tm=f sḏm "if he does not hear" is a condition: jr already holds the head of the clause, so the negation moves into the verb, tm. The same thinking explains r tm and tm in participles.

Skipping tm as an unknown word. Leave it out and jr tm=k sḏm turns into "if you listen", the opposite of what it says. Check: whenever tm appears, the sentence is negative, and the verb right after it is what is not done.
